blocks.content: Any feature of interest for the marginals can be computed from the m realizations of the Gibbs sequence. If $ \theta_1, \cdots, \theta_m $ is an appropriately burned-in set of realizations from a Gibbs sampler, the expectation of any function, $ f $, of the random variable $ \theta $ is approximated by $$ E[f(\theta)]_{m}=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}f(\theta_{i}) $$

This is the Monte-Carlo (MC) estimate of $ f(x) $, as $ E[f(\theta)]_m \to E[f(\theta)] $ as $ m \to \infty $. Likewise, the MC estimate for any function of $ n $ variables $ (\theta^{(1)}, \cdots, \theta^{(n)}) $ is calculated by $$ E[f(\theta^{(1)},\cdots,\theta^{(n)})]_{m}=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}f(\theta_{i}^{(1)},\cdots,\theta_{i}^{(n)}) $$
